issue.title: tui_perf.md: never paint a whole document into one Static; use a Line-API ScrollView

task_type_fields.proposed_change: Proposed by sase-1es.8 (note #2). Epic sase-1es (plan:202610/pager_performance.md) required this follow-up. Add a rule to `tui_perf.md`: "Never paint a whole document into one `Static`. Textual's Static renders and caches strips for every row of its renderable; the compositor does not virtualize rows of one big renderable. For long content, use a Line-API `ScrollView` (`render_line`, `virtual_size`, a bounded strip LRU), like `src/sase/pager/_screen_widgets.py` `PagerBodyScroll`." Evidence: on master before sase-1es, a 2,000-line pager mount made about 486k `Text.__rich_console__` calls and took 14s. A 20k-line open took 145s and 5.7GB. After the ScrollView swap (54427ed47c), 2k mounts in about 0.8s and 20k RSS is about 150MB. Also correct any remaining "one big renderable is virtualized" wording in memory. The src-side `_layout.py` docstring was already rewritten in 54427ed47c. Related but separate: sase-1f2 adds sase-1ez rules to the same note.

issue.creation_reason: Epic sase-1es proved Textual does not virtualize rows of one big Static renderable (the root cause of 14s/145s pager opens) and its plan requires recording that rule in tui_perf.md.

payload.description: Both add rules to tui_perf.md; coordinate edits to the same note
